requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to put each new or changed requirement into a group, where a group holds requirements that cite each other or describe one feature. It MUST direct them to review every group with its own read-only subagent, with all the reviews running in parallel, before presenting any group to the user.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.review` has no structural obligations. It says what the `habeas-requirements` skill must direct agents to do. Agents must put each new or changed requirement into a group, where a group holds requirements that cite each other or describe one feature. They must review every group with its own read-only subagent, with all reviews running in parallel, and they must do this before presenting any group to the user. These clauses describe what the skill's instructions say. They don't name a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface that the implementation must use or delegate to. The only candidate root is `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, which is the document that carries the directions. Any wording, section layout, or file organization that gives the same directions would satisfy the text equally. For example, the directions could sit in `section[Workflow]` or in another section. Section placement is therefore discretionary, so the requirement needs no `{impl}` marker on a structural root. Whether the skill's wording actually contains these directions is a behavioral and content question. It is not part of this structural assessment.

behavioral: The requirement sets documentation-directive obligations on the bundled skill `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`. Its Workflow step 3 holds the text.

The obligations, and the assertions in `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_reviews_each_group_with_a_parallel_read_only_subagent]` that cover them:

1. **Group the requirements.** The skill must direct agents to put each new or changed requirement into a group, where a group holds requirements that cite each other or describe one feature.
   - The test finds the review step with `step_of(SKILL, "start a read-only subagent")`.
   - It asserts that the step contains "Sort the new and changed requirements into groups".
   - It asserts that the step contains "requirements that cite each other or describe one feature".
2. **One read-only subagent per group, all in parallel.**
   - The test asserts that the step contains "For each group, start a read-only subagent, all in parallel".
   - That phrase covers per-group review, read-only, and parallel.
   - The step lookup itself keys on "start a read-only subagent".
3. **Review before presenting any group to the user.**
   - The test asserts `review < step_of(SKILL, "Present each group to the user")`.
   - That checks the ordering across numbered workflow steps. `step_of` panics if the presenting step is missing.

The helpers `workflow_steps`, `step`, `step_of` and `assert_text` parse the numbered Workflow steps and assert that each phrase is present. A rewording or dropped clause would fail the test. I read the skill paragraph, and it contains these phrases.

The obligations are directives in the skill text, so a text-presence test is the right kind of evidence. I found no untested obligation and no marking gap.
